## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #10351

Reviewed against `origin/main`, not against the report. Flipped ready, auto-merge armed. One file, +410/−63, no product code.

### The premise correction is the part I most wanted, and it was done the right way

I dispatched this saying the ratchet *should* be re-derivable to 0 now that #9936 landed — but that whether it had actually been stepped down was **a fact about the file, not an inference from the card being closed**, and that this seat had been burned twice today by exactly that confusion.

It was checked, and the answer is reported as a **half-falsified premise** rather than buried:

- *Still enumerated* — **yes**. `IHTTP_ROUTE_MODULES` was hand-named with no walk.
- *Ratchet still at 1* — **no**. Already stepped down.

Verified independently: `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs:728` on `origin/main` reads `'packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts': {}`. Confirmed.

### The false-positive measurement earned the full sweep

Triage's sizing note said the discriminator's false-positive surface was unmeasured and had to be measured **before** sweeping. It was, and the numbers are what make a full sweep affordable instead of a narrower shape:

| discriminator | files swept | false positives |
|---|---|---|
| receiver `res` only | 20 | **13** pure fetch readers (65%) |
| argument count only | 18 | **11** DSL files (`Field.json({…})`, `t.json(c.name)`) |
| both (shipped) | 7 | **0** |

Row 1's **20 reproduces the card's own "~20 `res.json(` files measured on main"** exactly — which is the check that the new scanner sees the same world the card measured, before it is trusted on files nobody enumerated.

### Where my own cross-check was the cruder instrument

I counted independently and got **13** write files against their 7, which I had to resolve before accepting. Six of my thirteen turn out to be **JSDoc comments and `note:` string literals** — `anonymous-deny.ts`, `plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`, `package-routes.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts`, `admin-routes.ts`, `spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts` — every one of which my line-based regex matched inside prose and their `ts.createSourceFile` parse correctly ignores. Same explanation for `rest-server.ts` reading 201 to my regex and 137 to theirs.

**7 real writers − 3 excluded as surface 1 = 4 audited**, which is exactly the audit table. I also independently confirm the structural claim that **no file mixes reads and writes**. Their measurement is right; mine was the coarser one.

### The reject side is asserted positively, which is the whole game

> The reject side is asserted **positively** as `reads: 1`, not as `bodies: 0` — a scanner that had simply stopped matching the receiver produces `bodies: 0` too.

That is the anti-vacuity discipline applied without being told, to the exact place it matters. Same for printing the reject side in the audit (`13 file(s) skipped as fetch readers, 83 zero-argument calls`) — a walk can otherwise only ever show what it swept **in**, so a silently-shrinking population looks identical to a clean one.

**M4 as a permanent self-test pin** is the other thing worth keeping: *the walk must re-find every declared express module*. That is reproduce-before-believing turned into a standing assertion rather than a one-off check.

Honest about the ablation table too — M5 and M6 are green on `--self-test` and the report says why (*a table fact, not a scanner fact*) instead of quietly presenting six red rows.

### The finding this walk was built for

Two files invisible to all four surfaces, now ratcheted: `packages/rest/src/query-allowlist.ts:194` and `query-multiplicity.ts:139`. Their shared 400 refusals are ADR-0112-nested already but carry no `success` above them, so `unwrapResponse` hands callers raw bodies. Neither is a route module and neither follows the `*-routes.ts` convention — which is precisely why an enumerated population never caught them.

⛔ Correctly **not** converted here: those ratchet against **#9559**, the standing owner of `packages/rest`'s convergence onto `sendOk`/`sendError`. Fixing the wire answers is that line's work.

Surfaces 1–3 are unmoved by the scanner change (10 route modules, 16 dispatcher domains, 11 Hono modules / 165 bodies, identical to the `736cfb14` baseline) — the no-collateral evidence for touching a shared scanner.

`Clause ②` answered: path limb is `packages/spec/src/**` and nothing here is under it; content limb changes a **lint gate's** accept/reject, not a wire contract. `skip-changeset` — root `scripts/` publishes nothing.
